canonical_question: What specific grain size range qualifies as 'nano-crystalline' for this specific W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy before irradiation?

question_variants.question: What specific grain size range qualifies as 'nano-crystalline' for this specific W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy before irradiation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text mentions the material preserved 'nano-crystallinity' and showed a '10 nm change in grain size', but does not provide the specific initial grain size range that defines the 'nano-crystalline' state for this specific alloy.

answers.answer: The document states that the material preserved its nano-crystallinity and showed only approximately 10 nm change in grain size after He implantation, but it does not specify the absolute grain size range (e.g., < 100 nm) that qualifies the material as 'nano-crystalline' before irradiation.
answers.conditions: Dual-beam irradiation (He + heavy ions) at 1173 K
answers.measurement_outcome: Approximately 10 nm change in grain size
answers.boundary_limitation: The specific grain size values defining 'nano-crystalline' are not provided.
evidence_spans: The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.
The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time

source_evidence_spans: the material preserved its nano-crystallinity and showed only approximately 10 nm change in grain size after ~8.45 at.% He implantation
